findings.problem: The simp set for `extEquivCohomologyClass` is asymmetric. For the inverse direction there are simp lemmas for `+`, `-`, negation, zero and `•` (`extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_add`, `_sub`, `_neg`, `_zero`, `_smul`). For the forward direction (`Ext X Y n → CohomologyClass`) there are simp lemmas for `+`, `-`, negation and zero, but none for `•`. A goal such as `R.extEquivCohomologyClass (r • α)` therefore does not normalise to `r • R.extEquivCohomologyClass α` under simp. It stays stuck, even though the analogous goals for `α + β`, `-α` and `0` simplify. The file already has a linear structure (`extLinearEquivCohomologyClass`), so the `•` case is the natural one to expect.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a forward-direction simp lemma next to `extEquivCohomologyClass_neg`:
```lean
@[simp]
lemma extEquivCohomologyClass_smul {R₀ : Type*} [Ring R₀] [Linear R₀ C] (r : R₀) (x : Ext X Y n) :
    R.extEquivCohomologyClass (r • x) = r • R.extEquivCohomologyClass x :=
  (R.extLinearEquivCohomologyClass (R₀ := R₀)).map_smul r x
```
The lemma can go after `extLinearEquivCohomologyClass`. Alternatively, prove it from `extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_smul` using `Equiv.symm_apply_eq` or `Equiv.apply_symm_apply`. This makes the forward rules complete, matching add/sub/neg/zero.
findings.benefit: Users computing in `Ext` through an injective resolution get uniform simp normalisation of `R.extEquivCohomologyClass` on all linear operations. They no longer have to switch to `.symm` form or build the linear equivalence by hand when a scalar appears. The forward and inverse simp interfaces become symmetric.
